text:
maria: Heads up — infra repo CI is hanging on Terraform plan for PR #412. `restore-cache` step stuck ~10m, runners pile up. https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/412 :eyes:
ryan: ugh saw a couple of flakes this morning too. can you paste the job link?
maria: https://github.com/redwood/infra/actions/runs/1234567890 — shows `actions/cache@v3` restore waiting. logs end with `Waiting for cache server...`
infra-bot: Workflow run queued: concurrency group `infra-plan` (max 2) reached — 3 runs waiting
jen: we hit the concurrency ceiling again after the scheduled dedicated-runner maintenance. might be starvation on self-hosted runners (us-west1).
maria: also seeing `terraform init` eventually times out after the cache hangs, so plan never runs.
ashley: any recent changes to the cache key logic in actions? last week we added repo + tfstate checksum.
ryan: no changes afaik. suspect the runner network egress to actions cache is problematic. had a brief outage in the region earlier per cloud console.
oncall: alert triggered: `infra-ci: long-running workflow` — 3 occurrences in the last 24h.
jen: quick mitigation: I'm going to re-run the blocked jobs with CACHE_DISABLED=1 to skip restore and confirm plan completes.
maria: please do. if that works we can revert to S3-backed cache or switch to `restore-keys` narrower matches.
jen: re-run started. logs: `Skipping cache restore because CACHE_DISABLED=true` -> terraform init -> plan succeeded in ~45s. :tada:
ryan: ok that proves restore is the culprit. long-term we should move the terraform artifact caching out of actions/cache onto our artifact service or use the cloud cache mirror.
ashley: also observed `helm lint` step in other jobs sometimes stalls with TLS handshake errors to chartmuseum. may be correlated with the same networking blips.
maria: proposal: 1) temporarily increase concurrency limit for `infra-plan` to 4, 2) disable cache for plan workflows until we migrate, 3) schedule a runner scale-up in us-west1 for next week.
oncall: note: increasing concurrency without more runners will just increase queue depth — recommend scaling runners first.
jen: created PR to set CACHE_DISABLED=1 for plan workflow and a rollback PR for when we have a stable cache: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/413
ryan: can we add a health-check step before cache restore that pings cache endpoint and fails fast if unreachable? avoid 10m hangs.
maria: good idea — add a 10s curl probe and if it fails fallback to skip restore. I'll draft a tiny action step.
jen: FYI I filed an infra ticket to evaluate moving cache to internal S3 mirror: INFRA-278
ashley: +1. also tagging eng-infra on the cloud incident that reported transient NAT gateway spikes earlier today. might be root cause.
maria: thanks everyone. action items: jen toggles CACHE_DISABLED for plan (PR merged), maria adds probe step, ops to check runner capacity and NAT gateway metrics. I'll follow up in the morning with post-mortem blurb for all-hands if this becomes recurring. :slightly_smiling_face:
